name: Gareth Mercer
life: “I still remember taking a new road alone for the first time.” On Thursday, near Tideline Market, Gareth picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I am the student who got the lesson. My employer tried to take the credit and I quietly corrected the newsletter.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an olive canvas jacket and a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. Gareth has a straight nose and deep-set eyes, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Gareth leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations during a conversation.
personality: Gareth enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Gareth is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
agenda: To correct the employer's claim to the lesson.
family: Barbara Jackson is Gareth’s half-sibling. Gareth calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Barbara leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The expensive summer*, Barbara says, “I carry plates and survive on tips. The dessert table stayed two hours and tipped me in four currencies.”
connections: Desmond Calloway. Job applicants who can drive still have to find a fair way to be tested. Also in the story is Malcolm Garrett (instructor).

reactions.situation: Someone asks whether the grant might buy a bus pass instead
reactions.response: Gareth prices a usable bus pass before dismissing it as a different kind of grant.

reactions.response: Gareth asks where they stood and what they could hear, leaving the rest open instead of filling it with guesses.
